Formulation  
Patient with known history of eczema presents with acute flare-up characterized by intense pruritus, soreness, and cracked skin involving chest, hands, and elbows. Symptoms severely disrupt sleep and concentration, causing distress and limiting activities. No new triggers identified; partial response to prior treatments noted. Psychosocial stress linked to symptom burden and impaired function at work and home. Protective factors include stable housing, employment, and insight into condition.  

Mental Health Care Plan Details  

Principal Problem: Eczema flare-up with severe itching and skin soreness  
- Patient Goal(s): Achieve symptomatic relief to restore sleep, concentration, and daily function; identify potential triggers  
- Clinical Goal(s): Control eczema flare with appropriate pharmacologic treatment; improve quality of life and symptom management  
- Actions (Patient): Use prescribed topical steroid and emollients regularly for 7-10 days; initiate prescribed oral antihistamine (Fexofenadine); maintain diary to identify possible triggers; return for follow-up if symptoms persist or worsen  
- Actions (Clinician/GP): Prescribe stronger topical steroid and Fexofenadine; provide emollient recommendations; advise on use of antihistamines; educate on trigger identification and diary keeping; schedule follow-up in one week  

Secondary Problem: Not recorded  

Patient Education, Emergency Care & Relapse Prevention  
- Education Given: Yes  
- Topics Covered: Proper use of topical steroids and emollients; antihistamine options; importance of moisturizing skin; keeping diary of potential triggers; when to seek further care  
- Early Warning Signs of Relapse/Worsening: Increased itchiness, skin cracking, spread of rash, sleep disturbance, or lack of response to treatment  
- Coping Strategies: Regular skin care, avoidance of irritants, use of antihistamines, monitoring symptoms and triggers
